steps.prompt: What is the last digit of $7^{100}$? Write the last digits of $7, 7^2, 7^3, 7^4, 7^5$ first. What do you see?

cards.title: Small cases, then the cycle
cards.body: When a question asks about a huge term, work out small cases until they repeat. Find the cycle length, then use the remainder. The last digits of powers repeat in cycles of length $1$, $2$ or $4$: for $3$ they go $3, 9, 7, 1, 3, 9, 7, 1, \ldots$

cards.title: Worked example: the last digit
cards.problem: What is the last digit of $3^{2026}$?

steps.text: The last digits of $3^1, 3^2, 3^3, 3^4$ are $3, 9, 7, 1$, then they repeat: the cycle has length $4$.

try.prompt: What is the remainder when $2026$ is divided by $4$?

steps.text: Remainder $2$ means the same last digit as $3^2$: $9$.

try.prompt: What is the last digit of $3^{2026}$?

cards.title: Remainder zero is the END of the cycle
cards.body: In a cycle of length $k$, term $n$ matches the term with position $n \bmod k$, except that remainder $0$ means the LAST one in the cycle. For number patterns, look at the differences: constant first differences mean arithmetic; constant second differences mean a quadratic like $n^2$ or $\frac{n(n + 1)}{2}$.

cards.title: Worked example: remainder zero
cards.problem: Lights flash red, green, blue, yellow, red, green, … What colour is the $100$th flash?

try.prompt: What is the remainder when $100$ is divided by $4$?

steps.text: Remainder $0$ means the LAST colour of the cycle: the 100th flash is yellow, colour number $4$.

try.prompt: Which colour number (red $1$, green $2$, blue $3$, yellow $4$)?

cards.title: The common trap: trusting too few terms
cards.body: Remainder $0$ is the last item of the cycle, not the first. Make sure the cycle really starts at term $1$ (some sequences settle into a cycle later). And check a pattern on enough terms: $1, 2, 4$ could continue $8$ or $7$.

prompts: What will you do first next time a problem asks about the $2026$th term of something?
